records.text: The scan shows the printed page number 804 and the 包部 / 包 bāo headword. Zhou Baohong calls 包 a 会意字, reads 勹 as wrapping and 巳 as an unborn child, and says they together express 胞衣. He also proposes that 包 should have existed in the Western Zhou because it occurs in the Shijing, while stating that it is not found in Shang or Western Zhou writing in his account. This is his received-form analysis and dating proposal, not independent proof of an early artifact or first attestation. The entry ends before the separate 胞 headword.

records.source: Li Xueqin (李學勤), chief editor, 字源, 2012; direct inspection of supplied scan
records.field: PDF p. 817, printed p. 804; separate 胞 headword immediately following 包; attached scan 1, decoded RGB pixel SHA-256 6630e899bbb88b4e0eb8017c00cef031d729588b5e64fdac8817a14916b66304
records.text: The separate 胞 entry calls 胞 a phono-semantic compound, quotes 說文 as deriving it from 肉 and 包, and reports Zhou Baohong’s estimate that 包 arose around Western Zhou while 胞 arose around Warring States to Han. These are claims about the 包/胞 relationship in the 胞 entry and must not be assigned to 勹’s role in 包.

records.field: PDF p. 814, printed p. 801; 勹部 / 勹 headword and entry; attached scan 3, decoded RGB pixel SHA-256 8a2d95408394358e8be286890d9cf9409cee5dc314189aa0ace9874275f10ec1; /home/catalin/hanzi-etymology-books/research-ocr/ziyuan-full/page-0814/source.png
records.text: The scan shows 勹部, 勹 bāo, and its separate entry. Zhou calls it a 会意字, quotes the Shuowen wrapping explanation, rejects derivations from 伏 or 旬 as unsupported, and says 勹 has its own source. He says texts used 包 in place of 勹 and describes 勹 and 包 as ancient/current forms of one another. This supports a separate account of 勹 and its later relationship with 包; it does not itself state that 勹 is phonetic in the 包 headword.
